21540-high-noon-a-new-sequel-to-three-we.creator: Unknown
21540-high-noon-a-new-sequel-to-three-we.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Towards Paradise, then, thundered the afternoon express from Paris, bearing the advance guard of the summer seekers after happiness. But if the cumbrous coaches carried swiftly onward some gay hearts, some young lovers to never-to-be-forgotten scenes, one there was among the throng to whom the world was gray--an English gentleman this, who gazed indifferently upon the bright vistas flitting past his window. The _London Times_ reposed unopened by his side; _Punch_, _Le Figaro_, _Jugend_ had pleased him not and tumbled to the floor unnoticed.

arxiv-1607-05540.title: Exploiting Vagueness for Multi-Agent Consensus
arxiv-1607-05540.creator: Michael Crosscombe, Jonathan Lawry Department of Engineering Mathematics, University of Bristol, BS8 1UB, United Kingdom m.crosscombe@bristol.ac.uk ⋅ \cdot j.lawry@bristol.ac.uk
arxiv-1607-05540.description: Abstract A framework for consensus modelling is introduced using Kleene’s three valued logic as a means to express vagueness in agents’ beliefs. Explicitly borderline cases are inherent to propositions involving vague concepts where sentences of a propositional language may be absolutely true , absolutely false or borderline .

arxiv-2111-04665.title: Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty and Robustness to Distributional Shift Using Real World Data
arxiv-2111-04665.creator: Kumud Lakara, Akshat Bhandari, Pratinav Seth, Ujjwal Verma
arxiv-2111-04665.description: Abstract Most machine learning models operate under the assumption that the training, testing and deployment data is independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.). This assumption does not generally hold true in a natural setting. Usually, the deployment data is subject to various types of distributional shifts.

arxiv-2207-06632.title: Theory of rigidity and numerical analysis of density of states of two-dimensional amorphous solids with dispersed frictional grains in the linear response regime
arxiv-2207-06632.creator: Daisuke Ishima 1, Kuniyasu Saitoh 2 , Michio Otsuki 3 and Hisao Hayakawa 1
arxiv-2207-06632.description: Abstract Using the Jacobian matrix, we obtain theoretical expression of rigidity and the density of states of two-dimensional amorphous solids consisting of frictional grains in the linear response to an infinitesimal strain, in which we ignore the dynamical friction caused by the slip processes of contact points. The theoretical rigidity agrees with that obtained by molecular dynamics simulations.

arxiv-2211-12441.title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
arxiv-2211-12441.creator: Ivan Hu, Dieter van Melkebeek, Andrew Morgan
arxiv-2211-12441.description: Abstract Given a rooted tree and a ranking of its leaves, what is the minimum number of inversions of the leaves that can be attained by ordering the tree? This variation of the well-known problem of counting inversions in arrays originated in mathematical psychology.

arxiv-2303-11853.title: LoRCoN-LO: Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Network-based LiDAR Odometry Thanks: All authors are with Seoul National University, South Korea, and D. Jung is with Smart City Engineering major, and Integrated Major in Smart City Global Convergence.
arxiv-2303-11853.creator: Donghwi Jung, Jae-Kyung Cho, Younghwa Jung, Soohyun Shin, Seong-Woo Kim
arxiv-2303-11853.description: Abstract We propose a deep learning-based LiDAR odometry estimation method called LoRCoN-LO that utilizes the long-term recurrent convolutional network (LRCN) structure. The LRCN layer is a structure that can process spatial and temporal information at once by using both CNN and LSTM layers.

arxiv-2304-06003.title: Approximation by a special de la Vallée Poussin type matrix transform mean of Walsh-Fourier series
arxiv-2304-06003.creator: István Blahota
arxiv-2304-06003.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider norm convergence for a special matrix-based de la Vallée Poussin-like mean of Fourier series for the Walsh system. We estimate the difference between the named mean above and the corresponding function in norm, and the upper estimation is given by the modulus of continuity of the function. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 42C10 1.

arxiv-2305-18012.title: Large-scale turbulent driving regulates star formation in high-redshift gas-rich galaxies II: Influence of the magnetic field and the turbulent compressive fraction
arxiv-2305-18012.creator: Noé Brucy, Patrick Hennebelle, Tine Colman, Simon Iteanu
arxiv-2305-18012.description: Abstract Context. The observed star formation rate (SFR) in galaxies is well below what it should be if gravitational collapse alone were at play. There is still no consensus about the main process that cause the regulation of the SFR. Aims.

arxiv-2409-03143.title: Large Étendue 3D Holographic Display with Content-adaptive Dynamic Fourier Modulation
arxiv-2409-03143.creator: Brian Chao, Manu Gopakumar, Suyeon Choi, Jonghyun Kim, Liang Shi, Gordon Wetzstein
arxiv-2409-03143.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Brian Chao, Manu Gopakumar, Suyeon Choi, Jonghyun Kim, Liang Shi, Gordon Wetzstein. Emerging holographic display technology offers unique capabilities for next-generation virtual reality systems. Current holographic near-eye displays, however, only support a small étendue, which results in a direct tradeoff between achievable field of view and eyebox size. Étendue expansion has recently been explored, but existing approaches are either fundamentally limited in the image quality that can be achieved or they require extremely high-speed spatial light modulators.

arxiv-2410-22269.title: Fourier Head: Helping Large Language Models Learn Complex Probability Distributions
arxiv-2410-22269.creator: Nate Gillman, Daksh Aggarwal, Michael Freeman, Saurabh Singh, Chen Sun
arxiv-2410-22269.description: Abstract As the quality of large language models has improved, there has been increased interest in using them to model non-linguistic tokens. For example, the Decision Transformer recasts agentic decision making as a sequence modeling problem, using a decoder-only LLM to model the distribution over the discrete action space for an Atari agent.

arxiv-2512-07986.description: Abstract . We describe germs of mappings ( ℂ 2 , 0 ) → ( ℂ 2 , 0 ) (\mathbb{C}^{2},0)\to(\mathbb{C}^{2},0) ramified along a germ of irreducible curve whose image is of the form x p = y q x^{p}=y^{q} . This paper is an addendum to Kulikov’s paper [ 6 ] .

pmc-10545796.title: HCG supplement did not accelerate tunica albuginea remodeling to facilitate penile growth
pmc-10545796.creator: Tao Li, Yuan Tian, Quliang Zhong, Peng Chen, Junhao Zhang, Guangshi Du, Lei Li, Yiting Jiang, Kehua Jiang
pmc-10545796.description: Penile size is closely concerned and short penis contributes serious sexual dysfunction and tremendous psychological problems to couples. Androgen is essential for penile development and testosterone replacement is recommended to patients with micropenis. We previously proved that inhibiting activity of lysyl oxidase (Anti-lysyl oxidase, Anti-LOX) combined with vacuum erectile device (VED) lengthened penis by remodeling tunica albuginea.

pmc-10824985.title: Current situation and trend of non-coding RNA in rheumatoid arthritis: a review and bibliometric analysis
pmc-10824985.creator: Zehong Wei, Huaiyu Li, Senhao Lv, Junping Yang
pmc-10824985.description: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune disease that affects multiple joints and has adverse effects on various organs throughout the body, often leading to a poor prognosis. Recent studies have shown significant progress in the research of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) in RA.

pmc-11354234.title: Cracking the Codes behind Cancer Cells’ Immune Evasion
pmc-11354234.creator: Nikita Mundhara, Pritam Sadhukhan
pmc-11354234.description: Immune evasion is a key phenomenon in understanding tumor recurrence, metastasis, and other critical steps in tumor progression. The tumor microenvironment (TME) is in constant flux due to the tumor’s ability to release signals that affect it, while immune cells within it can impact cancer cell behavior.

pmc-11425727.title: Analysis of Serum Bile Acid Profile Characteristics and Identification of New Biomarkers in Lean Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease Based on LC-MS/MS
pmc-11425727.creator: Bing Wang, Fei Zhang, Hong Qiu, Yujie He, Haotian Shi, Yuerong Zhu
pmc-11425727.description: Objectives:Plasma bile acid (BA) has been widely studied as pathophysiological factors in chronic liver disease. But the changes of plasma BA level in lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) remains unclear. Here, we clarified the BA metabolic characteristics of lean MAFLD and explored its significance and mechanism as a marker.

pmc-11627428.title: Integration of pharmacophore-based virtual screening, molecular docking, ADMET analysis, and MD simulation for targeting EGFR: A comprehensive drug discovery study using commercial databases
pmc-11627428.creator: Abdullah R. Alanzi, Ashaimaa Y. Moussa, Mohammed S. Alsalhi, Tayyab Nawaz, Ijaz Ali
pmc-11627428.description: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), a crucial component of cellular signaling pathways, is frequently dysregulated in a range of cancers. EGFR targeting has become a viable approach in the development of anti-cancer medications. This study employs an integrated approach to drug discovery, combining multiple computational methodologies to identify potential EGFR inhibitors.

pmc-11653768.title: Investigating the causes of maternal mortality in Razavi Khorasan based on forensic medical records during the years 2015 to 2022
pmc-11653768.creator: Tahereh Fathi Najafi, Sareh Dashti, Ali Naghsh, Maryam Saboor Parsa
pmc-11653768.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMaternal mortality is among the main indicators of health in nations. Identifying the causes of maternal mortality is crucial in designing preventive interventions. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the causes of maternal mortality during 8 years.MethodsThis descriptive-analytical study was conducted on the archived cases of maternal mortality in the Forensic Medicine Department of the Khorasan Razavi Province between March 2013 and March 2022, but as no data was available for the first two years, maternal mortality data for 8 years was

pmc-12519791.title: Evaluation of Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. mycoides antigens capable of stimulating host IRG-47 release identifies Mmm604, Mmm605, and Mmm606 as potential subunit vaccine antigens
pmc-12519791.creator: Tong Liu, Huanjun Zhao, Qi Wu, Yukun Wei, Jiuqing Xin, Qiao Pan
pmc-12519791.description: Contagious bovine pleuropneumonia (CBPP), caused by Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. mycoides (Mmm), is a devastating cattle disease with high morbidity and mortality, threatening cattle productivity in Sub-Saharan Africa and potentially in parts of Asia. Cross-border livestock trade increases the risk of CBPP introduction or reintroduction.

pmc-12625164.title: Mitigate Japan's Drug Loss With Model‐Informed Drug Development
pmc-12625164.creator: Yasuhiko Imai, Emi Akatsu, Suzanne K Minton
pmc-12625164.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ‘Drug loss’ in Japan refers to drugs that have been approved and marketed overseas but haven't been developed, submitted, or approved in Japan. A comprehensive Model‐Informed Drug Development (MIDD) strategy, enhanced with artificial intelligence/machine learning, can minimize drug loss.

pmc-12664912.title: Femoral arteriovenous concentration differences reveal metabolomic shifts in peripheral artery disease (PAD): A case–control study
pmc-12664912.creator: Tuljo Ööbik, Jaak Kals, Jaan Eha, Mihkel Zilmer, Kalle Kilk, Kaido Paapstel
pmc-12664912.description: Background:We aimed to investigate metabolomic alterations in peripheral artery disease (PAD) by analyzing blood from the femoral artery and vein, assessing metabolite release/uptake in chronically ischemic lower limbs (PAD group) and nonischemic limbs (controls), and evaluating the representativeness of upper-limb venous samples.

pmc-12830511.title: Laparoscopic vs open gastrectomy after neoadjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced gastric cancer: comparative short- and long-term outcomes
pmc-12830511.creator: Mingtao Liang, Jianan Tan, Shengning Zhou, Pengliang Wang, Yequan Xie, Guangyu Zhong, Dejiang Zhou, Fanghai Han, Bin Yang
pmc-12830511.description: BackgroundLaparoscopic gastrectomy (LG) represents a technically challenging procedure for locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). The safety and efficacy profiles of LG following NAC remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to compare short- and long-term outcomes between LG and open gastrectomy (OG) in NAC-treated LAGC patients.

pmc-13068968.title: Unsaponifiable fraction of black Vitis vinifera seed oil attenuates liver cancer progression by targeting apoptosis and key tumor-associated genes: In vitro, in vivo, and in silico studies
pmc-13068968.creator: Marwa M. Abu-Serie, Ashraf A. El-Faham, Ghada M. Ahmad, Noha H. Habashy
pmc-13068968.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cancer is the leading cause of death worldwide. This study evaluated the anti-liver cancer influence of the unsaponifiable fraction (UnSap) derived from black Vitis vinifera seed oil (BVVO) using the HepG-2 cell line and a HCC mouse model. Compared with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), UnSap exhibited a strong antioxidant capacity, excellent safety (in PBMCs), and a higher selectivity index (SI) with a lower IC₅₀ against HepG-2 cells. It effectively induced apoptosis and modulated the expression of key genes involved in cell cycle progression.

pmc-13182084.title: Validity and responsiveness of the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-9 to measure health and wellbeing impact of heatwaves among older adults
pmc-13182084.creator: Meixia Liao, Fanni Rencz, Zhihao Yang, Jianjun Xiang, Nan Luo
pmc-13182084.description: BackgroundThe health impact of heatwaves is usually assessed using mortality, morbidity and healthcare service utilization. This study explored the feasibility of using subjective measures to capture and quantify the impact of heatwaves on the health and wellbeing of older adults.

pmc-13194748.title: Clinical impact of proteinuria and blood pressure variability on long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention
pmc-13194748.creator: Jongheon Jeong, Byung Sik Kim, Woohyeun Kim, Hyungdon Kook, Yonggu Lee, Jin-Kyu Park, Jeong-Hun Shin, Hwan-Cheol Park, Jinho Shin, Young-Hyo Lim
pmc-13194748.description: Proteinuria and blood pressure variability (BPV) are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes in coronary artery disease (CAD). However, their combined prognostic impact after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is unknown. To investigate the association of proteinuria and BPV with long-term outcomes after PCI, we analyzed 2,539 patients from an observational PCI registry.

pmc-13225561.title: Prevalence and long-term outcomes of brain fog and cognitive impairment in individuals with long COVID: A systematic review
pmc-13225561.creator: Ahmar Faseeh, Maryam Rida, Noor e Karim, Ayesha Zafar, Arif Shah, Abida Perveen
pmc-13225561.description: Background:Long COVID is increasingly recognized as a complex multisystem condition, with brain fog and cognitive impairment emerging as some of its manifestations. Despite growing literature, the pooled prevalence, subgroup differences, and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood.Methods:We systematically reviewed 47 studies (2000–2025) encompassing over 25,000 patients to evaluate the prevalence of brain fog and cognitive impairment among long COVID populations.

pmc-13251500.title: National surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in Iran using IAMR software: A hospital-based study
pmc-13251500.creator: Edris Hoseinzadeh, Hossein Masoumi-Asl
pmc-13251500.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global public health concern that requires standardized and context-specific surveillance systems to inform antimicrobial stewardship and clinical decision-making.ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate AMR patterns among inpatient and outpatient populations in a tertiary teaching hospital in central Iran and to assess the performance of the Iranian Antimicrobial Resistance Management (IAMR) system in generating stratified surveillance data.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted from September 2023 to July 2024 using routine clinical specimens.

pmc-13278721.title: A Novel Renal Manifestation in GLIS3-Related Disorder in a Pediatric Patient With Cystic Nephroma
pmc-13278721.creator: Ibrahim Alharbi, Danah Khalid Alharbi, Razan Abdelrahim, Bayan Fawaz Alzahrani
pmc-13278721.description: A 10-year-old Saudi girl with a homozygous GLIS3 gene deletion presented with the classic triad of neonatal diabetes mellitus, congenital hypothyroidism, and congenital glaucoma. During routine surveillance, an incidental complex left renal mass was identified. Comprehensive imaging and histopathological analysis following a core needle biopsy diagnosed a benign multicystic nephroma with features of a mixed epithelial and stromal tumor (MEST).

pmc-13347540.title: A longitudinal study on physical activity in early Parkinson's disease
pmc-13347540.creator: Samuel Yong-Ern Ng, Darakhshan Naheed, Ehsan Seyed Saffari, Nicole Shuang-Yu Chia, Xinyi Choi, Dede Liana Heng, Shermyn Xiu-Min Neo, Zheyu Xu, Kay-Yaw Tay, Wing-Lok Au, Eng-King Tan, Louis Chew-Seng Tan
pmc-13347540.description: Physical activity (PA) remains critical in the slowing of disease progression in early Parkinson's disease (PD), although the longitudinal follow-up of such studies remain scarce. Using data from an early PD Cohort, we longitudinally examined the impact of unprescribed PA on symptoms of early PD, controlling for demographics and medications.

pmc-13486663.creator: Yongbiao Zhai, Peijie Chen, Ying Luo, Ziyu Lv, Guanglong Ding, Junjie Yang, Minglin Zheng, Ye Zhou, Yang Chai, Su-Ting Han

pmc-13506840.title: Whole-genome characterisation of high-risk ST131 and the emerging ST1193 UPEC lineages in Romanian patients with recurrent urinary tract infections
pmc-13506840.creator: Laura-Ioana Popa, Sorin Dinu, Daniela Cristea, Andreea Ghiță, Gabriel Ionescu, Mihaela Oprea
pmc-13506840.description: Recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs) are frequently associated with persistent uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) lineages that combine antimicrobial resistance with virulence traits, contributing to treatment failure. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on 199 UPEC isolates recovered from patients with recurrent or difficult-to-treat UTIs for whom autovaccine therapy was recommended.

pmc-13545508.creator: Youming Huang, Qiong Bian, Yeyu Shen, Xiaoxia Ding, Yan Teng, Danfeng Xu, Xianhong Yang, Yibin Fan
pmc-13545508.description: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common form of non‐scarring hair loss, driven by genetic factors and increased sensitivity of scalp hair follicles to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which causes progressive miniaturization of dermal papilla cells and shortens the hair growth phase. The precise molecular pathogenesis of AGA remains incompletely understood.

pmc-13563113.title: Postburn Downregulation of miR‐148a‐3p and Its Regulatory Mechanism in Hypertrophic Scar Formation
pmc-13563113.creator: Yanhua Lu, Meng Yu, Jinghe Zhou, Yang Yang
pmc-13563113.description: BackgroundBurn injuries represent a common form of trauma, and their healing process poses a significant clinical challenge, frequently complicated by aberrant scarring. Recent studies have found that miR‐148a‐3p is an important regulator involved in the process of tissue fibrosis, but the specific mechanism of action of miR‐148a‐3p in burn wound repair still needs to be elucidated.
